title: perf(canary): adaptive latency detector + hysteresis rollout guard
author: Ethan Park
description:
Context: We occasionally observe transient p95 spikes during autoscaling and KV cache evictions that cause canary-based rollouts to oscillate (flap) or to prematurely abort traffic shifts. This PR introduces an adaptive latency detector that adjusts sensitivity based on recent distributional noise and a hysteresis-based rollout guard to prevent rapid rollback/forward cycles.

What it does (high level):
- Adds an adaptive detector (moving window + robust percentile smoothing) that computes dynamic thresholds for p50/p95/p99 with noise estimation.
- Adds a hysteresis rollout guard integrated with the rollout controller: decisions require sustained violation for N windows and require a stricter recovery condition to re-enable traffic.
- Exposes tuning flags (canary.window_size, canary.noise_factor, rollout.hysteresis_windows, rollout.recovery_multiplier) with safe defaults.
- Adds instrumentation (prometheus metrics + structured events) and end-to-end tests in the perf-canary pipeline.

Why: Static thresholds caused false positives on bursty workloads and on background GC/eviction events. The adaptive detector reduces manual threshold tuning and the hysteresis guard reduces flapping while preserving regression detection sensitivity.

Checklist: 
- [x] Detector algorithm implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Rollout guard logic + integration tests
- [x] Metrics and tracing added
- [x] Perf pipeline integration (perf-canary)
- [x] Documentation and config comments

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind canary.experimental_adaptive_detector=false by default. After merge we'll enable on a small subset of customers and run for 48h under observation (ENG-2031).

Related: Linear ENG-2031 (adaptive canary detection), ENG-2045 (rollout hysteresis design), incident SUP-1123
